question: Which of the following correctly lists the four guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) pillars for HFrEF (LVEF <40%) that reduce mortality?

answers.text: ACEi/ARNI + Beta-blocker + Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist + SGLT2 inhibitor

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. These four classes (exemplified by sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol/bisoprolol, spironolactone/eplerenone, empagliflozin/dapagliflozin) have proven survival benefit in RCTs (PARADIGM-HF, COPERNICUS, RALES/EMPHASIS, DAPA-HF/EMPEROR-Reduced) and form the current standard of care for HFrEF.

Incorrect. Digoxin and furosemide are symptom-controlling agents without proven mortality benefit in isolation. Amiodarone is not a pillar; it is reserved for refractory ventricular arrhythmias in HF.

Incorrect. Dihydropyridine CCBs have neutral or harmful effects in HFrEF (negative inotropy worsens pump function). Thiazides are used in hypertension, not as HF mortality drugs. This is an antihypertensive rather than an HF GDMT regimen.

Incorrect. Statins do not reduce mortality in HF (CORONA, GISSI-HF). Ivabradine reduces hospitalisation in selected patients (HR >70) but is not a first-line pillar. ARB alone (not ARNI) is second-tier.

overallFeedback.feedback: The four mortality-reducing pillars for HFrEF are: (1) ACEi or ARNI, (2) evidence-based beta-blocker (carvedilol, bisoprolol, metoprolol succinate), (3) MRA (spironolactone/eplerenone), and (4) SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin/empagliflozin).

Excellent. The four GDMT pillars — ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i — collectively reduce mortality by ~50–60% and are the foundation of HFrEF management. Every eligible patient with LVEF <40% should be on all four unless contraindicated.
